Convert a circle's general equation to standard form, identify center and radius, and determine whether it has real points.
The general equation is the expanded form of (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r². Completing the square reveals its center and radius.
D and E are the linear coefficients and F is the constant. A real circle needs positive squared radius.
Move F to the other side, complete both squares, and take the positive square root for r.
A negative r² means no real points; r²=0 gives a single point.
